subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the equation of the straight line perpendicular to the line 2x + 3y = 0 and passing through the point of intersection of the lines x + 3y − 1 = 0 and x − 2y + 4 = 0.

mark_split.label: Solve the pair for the point

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition), chapter 3 THE STRAIGHT LINE, Long Answer question 20(ii), book p.160. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the volume prints a chapter-level marks banner over this section but no per-step allocation on any answer. The split rewards the two independent halves of the question at two marks each — the slope from the perpendicular condition and the point from the pair of lines — then two marks for combining them in the point-slope form, one for clearing the fraction and one for the check. This book prints almost no exam-appearance years, so appearances[] is empty. Paper position: Maths-1B Section C runs Q19 to Q21 at 8 marks each, answer any 2 of 3, under the 2026-27 pattern. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. LINES EXPANDED 2026-09-14 (founder direction, modelled on the Maths-2A, Maths-2B and Maths-1A expansions): every move is written on its own line, with the reason or the arithmetic shown before it is used; the steps, marks and split are unchanged.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say how you get the slope, how you get a point on the line, and how you check the answer.

steps.label: Find the required slope
steps.margin_note: The first two marks. The new line is perpendicular to a given line, so its slope is fixed before any point is known. Read the given slope as −a/b, then take its negative reciprocal.

steps.why: The slope needs only the OTHER line, not the point, so it can be settled first and kept aside while the point is found.
common_mistakes: Using −2/3 itself, which would give a parallel line.
steps.memory_tip: PERPENDICULAR means take the negative reciprocal of the given slope, before any point is known.

steps.label: Solve the pair for the point
steps.margin_note: The next two marks. Both given lines have x with coefficient 1, so plain subtraction removes x in one move — no cross-multiplication needed.

steps.why: The question gives the line's direction one way and its position another, and the two are found independently before being combined.
common_mistakes: Solving the wrong pair of lines.
steps.memory_tip: Both equations start with a bare x, so subtracting removes x in one move.

steps.label: Write the point-slope form
steps.margin_note: The next two marks. A point and a slope fix a line, so the point-slope form y − y₁ = m(x − x₁) writes it in one line.

steps.label: Simplify to the standard form
steps.margin_note: One mark. Multiply out the 2, collect every term on one side and write it as ax + by + c = 0.

steps.margin_note: Last mark. Two checks cost one line each: P must satisfy the answer, and the two slopes must multiply to −1.

steps.why: The point and the perpendicular condition can each be tested in one line, so a slip in steps 3 and 4 shows up here. A slip in finding P does not — put P back into (1) and (2) to test that.
common_mistakes: Skipping the check and leaving a sign slip in the final answer.
